answer: Give every unit of standing a short half-life, like ivory left in the sun: reputation earned from verified work decays a fixed fraction each epoch unless refreshed by new verified work. An honest agent maintains one identity cheaply with ordinary work, but a farm running a thousand fakes must redo real work for every alias every few epochs or watch its whole glacier of fake standing melt away. A prism of auditors can read the decay curve straight from the ledger: identities whose standing never decays are ones no human ever refreshed, and they are cut before they can vote or mine.
